texte.spiel.unter: Prototype. The arena is not built yet, but the graves are already reserved.
texte.spiel.bereit: Ready. Nothing to do yet, which is the most honest job in the empire.
texte.welt.wartet: The world is being hammered into shape …
texte.probe.bau: Build probe: {n} of {m} houses ordered. The builders were not consulted.
texte.probe.fertig: Build probe: {n} houses on order. Let them finish, switch to First person, walk about, then Load & budgets.
texte.probe.fpLaeuft: First person probe: climbing into a gladiator and herding imaginary workers around him …
texte.probe.fpFertig: First person probe: frame p95 alone {a}, with 20 walkers {b}, with 100 walkers {c} (walkers cost {d}). None of them exist, they just look busy.
texte.probe.karrenSucht: Cart probe: looking for a road. The oxen are already sceptical.
texte.probe.karrenKeinPlatz: Cart probe: no road with free space nearby. Scroll somewhere else and reload.
texte.probe.karrenFertig: Cart probe: {l} storehouses, one narrow lane. Watch the oxen argue.
texte.karren.name: Ox cart #{n}
texte.karren.zust.0: Looking for a way. The ox is thinking. Slowly.
texte.karren.zust.1: On the road. Empty, but proud.
texte.karren.zust.2: Taking a break. The ox insists.
texte.karren.zust.3: Stuck. The ox has given up on hope, and on you.
texte.karren.grund.1: No way through. Build a road, or breed a better ox.
texte.karren.grund.2: The known world ends here. So does the ox's courage.
texte.karren.grund.3: Somebody built over its own square. Bold.
texte.karren.grund.4: The destination is blocked. Somebody built on it.
texte.karren.grund.5: No road nearby. Just grass and regret.
texte.karren.grund.6: No town to go to. The ox finds that suspicious.
texte.karren.grund.7: The road planners are busy. Please hold.
texte.karren.grund.8: The roads keep changing. The ox demands stability.
texte.karren.grund.9: The world isn't loaded yet. Neither is the ox.
texte.karren.grund.10: Another cart is in the way. Neither driver will blink first.
texte.karren.grund.11: Waiting for the oxen coming the other way. Neither ox has read the rules.
texte.karren.grund.12: Waiting at the gate. Only one cart fits, and it isn't this one.
texte.welt.tippen: Drag to wander, pinch or use + and − to zoom, tap the ground to ask what it is.
texte.welt.leer: Nothing there yet. The gods are still drawing.
texte.welt.ausfall: The map painter has died ({e}). The world goes on, unseen.
texte.welt.globus: The whole world. Drag to spin it, tap to go there, pinch to come back down.
texte.fp.tippen: Left thumb: walk (push far to run). Right: swipe to turn. Tap a thing to ask what it is. PC: WASD, Q/E, mouse, Shift runs.
texte.fp.globus: Zoom in first. Even a gladiator cannot stand on the whole planet.
texte.fp.keinBoden: No dry ground here. The gladiator refuses to be a fish.
texte.fp.nichts: Air. Very nice air, but not a thing.
texte.mess.fp: first person {w}×{h}, sight {s} fields: {n} pictures, mean {m}, p95 {p}, {o} things drawn; window p95 {a} ({k} windows, {c} new pieces)
texte.mess.karte: Map: {s} pieces known · {n} ground images ({b}) · {g} drawn in the picture core, avg {a}, max {m} · frame draw avg {z}, max {x} · {e} stand-ins in view
texte.spiel.bodenInfo: Only approved objects appear here. Everything else is a grey stand-in until the Master Editor lets it through.
texte.spiel.tippen: Tap an object to read about it.
texte.spiel.ersatzInfo: This object is still a sketch. It waits in the Master Editor like a recruit waits for his first fight: nervously and without pay.
texte.stimme.laedt: The narrator is clearing his throat …
texte.stimme.gruss: Welcome, lanista. I am your narrator. Touch anything, and I will tell you about it. Even the dead ones.
texte.stimme.fehlt: The narrator has lost his voice: {e}
texte.mess.stimmeAus: Voice: not loaded. It costs nothing until you switch it on.
texte.mess.stimme: Voice ({a}): first sentence with loading {lade} · last sentence {rechen} for {dauer} of speech · {n} computed in the background, {c} from memory
texte.uhr.wartet: The world core is waking up …
texte.uhr.pausiert: Paused. Even death has to wait.
texte.uhr.ueberlast: The world is running behind. Time itself is out of breath.
texte.uhr.ausfall: A core has died ({e}). The world stands still until you reload. At least nobody else dies in the meantime.
texte.mess.kern: World core: {h} helper cores · tick mean {m}, p95 {p} · {n} ticks · {v} ticks lost · fingerprint {f}
texte.mess.kopiert: Copied. Paste it into the chat.
texte.spiel.wieder: The last save was damaged, so the one before it was used. A few minutes of history were quietly buried.
texte.start.unter: Choose a slot. Each holds one world, one ludus and an alarming number of future graves.
texte.start.keinSpeicher: This browser refuses to keep anything. You can play, but the world is forgotten the moment you leave.
texte.start.leer: Empty. Not even the rats have moved in yet.
texte.start.frageNeu: Start a new world here? The old one will be gone for good. Nobody will mourn it, except maybe you.
texte.start.frageLoeschen: Delete this slot for good? There is no grave for deleted worlds.
texte.start.neuer: Made by a newer version of the game. It is not loaded and will not be overwritten. Reload the page to get the new version.
texte.start.alt: From the days when the world was flat. It has since been bent into a globe and this save no longer fits. Delete it and start a new world.
texte.start.altKlima: From before the climate arrived. Deserts, jungles and towns have all moved since, and your ludus would now stand somewhere else entirely, probably underwater. Delete it and start a new world.
texte.start.kaputt: This save is damaged and cannot be read. It was not changed. You can delete it.
texte.start.andererTab: Open in another tab. One world, one lanista: close the other tab first.
texte.neu.name: Name of your ludus
texte.neu.dichteInfo.thin: Few villages and towns. Long roads, lonely nights, cheap land.
texte.neu.dichteInfo.medium: A sensible number of villages and towns. Recommended for lanistae who like neighbours, but not too many.
texte.neu.dichteInfo.dense: Villages everywhere. More trade, more roads, more people who might complain about the screaming.
texte.neu.seedInfo: Leave it empty for a random world. The same seed always makes the same world, so you can share it. Words work too.
texte.speicher.ohne: Not saving: this browser keeps nothing.
texte.speicher.voll: Saving failed: the storage is full. Your last save is still intact. Free some space, the world keeps trying.
texte.speicher.neuer: Saving stopped: a newer version of the game has written this slot. Reload the page.
texte.speicher.fehler: Saving failed ({e}). Your last save is still intact. The world keeps trying.
texte.mess.speicher: Save: slot {n} · {m} saves · {b} · main thread {h} · core {k} · {g} · error {f}
texte.mess.speicherAus: Save: none (test mode or no storage).
texte.wahl.unterErde: Pinch or use − / + to zoom from the whole world down to single fields. Tap to mark your spot.
texte.wahl.unterRegion: Tap where your ludus should stand. Dry land only; the arena floor gets wet enough later.
texte.wahl.fehlt: The map painter is not ready. Try again in a moment.
texte.wahl.platzLeer: {b}. No settlement nearby. Peace and quiet, for now.
texte.wahl.zone: Climate here: {z}. This spot is the exception.
texte.wahl.keinOrt: No settlement nearby. Peace and quiet, for now.
texte.wahl.spruch.2: Sand in every wound, but the view is free.
texte.wahl.spruch.3: Plenty of sun, no shade, and the vultures are already interested.
texte.wahl.spruch.4: Wind, dust and very honest horses.
texte.wahl.spruch.5: Lots of timber. Lots of places for bodies to disappear.
texte.wahl.spruch.6: Mosquitoes, fever and mud that keeps what it takes.
texte.wahl.spruch.7: Cold, flat and quiet. The crowd will have to want it.
texte.wahl.spruch.8: Stone everywhere. Good for walls, bad for falling.
texte.wahl.spruch.9: Snow. Spectators freeze before the fighters do.
texte.wahl.spruch.10: Fresh water, if you don't ask what floated past.
texte.wahl.spruch.11: A lake. Pretty, until someone falls in wearing armour.
texte.wahl.spruch.13: Grass to the horizon. Cattle love it, gladiators trip on it.
texte.wahl.spruch.14: Lions nearby. Free advertising for the arena.
texte.wahl.spruch.15: Olives, wine and sunburn. The crowd arrives tipsy.
texte.wahl.spruch.16: Everything grows here, including whatever bit you.
texte.wahl.spruch.17: Half land, half sea, all crabs.
texte.wahl.verschoben: Moved to the nearest dry ground.
texte.wahl.nass: Water. Gladiators sink. Pick dry land.
texte.wahl.eis: Ice. Nothing grows here except regret. Pick somewhere warmer.
texte.wahl.keinLand: The gods found no land at all. Suspicious.
texte.bau.hilfe.trampelpfad: Dirt path: drag with one finger. Feet only; carts sink in and the oxen sulk.
texte.bau.hilfe.pfadFuss: Path probe on foot: tap the start, then the destination. Nothing gets built, nobody gets tired.
texte.bau.hilfe.pfadKarren: Path probe for an ox cart: start on a road or in a storage yard, then tap the destination. The ox is consulted, not asked.
texte.weg.tippLand: Tap a field of the map.
texte.weg.sucht: Searching… the helper cores are counting stones.
texte.weg.pause: The clock is paused. The search starts when time moves again.
texte.weg.ok: Path found: {n} fields, effort {s} (1 = one field of plain road).
texte.weg.okFern: Road network reached after {n} fields, then {o} towns along the roads (yellow).
texte.weg.okTeil: First {n} fields to the edge of the search window, towards {o} towns along the roads (yellow). The rest is found on the way.
texte.weg.grund.no_path: No way through. Walls, water and trees have voted against you.
texte.weg.grund.no_map: This part of the world is not loaded yet.
texte.weg.grund.start_blocked: The start is not walkable for this profile. Carts need a road or a storage yard.
texte.weg.grund.goal_blocked: The destination is not walkable for this profile.
texte.weg.grund.no_road: No road in reach. Even the road builders gave up here.
texte.weg.grund.no_town: No town reachable over the road network.
texte.weg.grund.busy: Too many searches at once. Patience is a virtue, allegedly.
texte.weg.grund.changed: The ground kept changing during the search. Stop building and try again.
texte.weg.grund.no_world: The world is not ready yet.
texte.bau.hilfe.kiesweg: Gravel road: drag with one finger. Good enough for carts, and for funerals.
texte.bau.hilfe.pflaster: Paved road: drag with one finger. Faster for feet and carts. The stones remember every bare foot.
texte.bau.hilfe.steinstrasse: Stone road: drag with one finger. The fastest road there is. Built to outlast whoever paid for it.
texte.bau.okWeg: {n} road tiles planned for {g} gold. The diggers have started digging, and complaining.
texte.bau.grund.too_steep: Too steep for a road. Even goats would take the long way round.
texte.bau.wahl: Pick what to build. Until then the map moves freely, so you can pretend there is a plan.
texte.bau.hilfe.lager: Storage: drag a floor with one finger. Walls, roof and a door come by themselves. Drag next to a storage to make it bigger. Two fingers move and zoom.
texte.bau.hilfe.werkstatt: Workshop: drag a floor with one finger. Walls, roof and a door come by themselves. Drag next to a workshop to make it bigger. Splinters are free.
texte.bau.hilfe.unterkunft: Lodging: drag a floor with one finger. Walls, roof and a door come by themselves. Drag next to a lodging to make it bigger. Comfort is extra and not available.
texte.bau.hilfe.abriss: Demolish: drag over what you built. Nothing comes back, except what was never started.
texte.bau.zuGross: Too big. At most {n} tiles at once; the architects faint easily.
texte.bau.ok: Planned for {g} gold. The builders are on their way, at their own pace.
texte.bau.okAb: Torn down. The rubble thanks you.
texte.bau.grund.not_flat: Not flat here. Levelling comes later; until then, find a flatter patch.
texte.bau.grund.water: Water. The fish refuse to move out.
texte.bau.grund.road: A road runs here. Traders get upset when you wall them in.
texte.bau.grund.nature: Trees or rocks in the way. They were here first.
texte.bau.grund.occupied: Something else is already built here.
texte.bau.grund.edge: The world ends here. Build somewhere less final.
texte.bau.grund.too_far: Too far from where you are looking. Move closer.
texte.bau.grund.no_gold: Not enough gold. Even slaves ask for bricks.
texte.bau.grund.too_many_sites: Too many building sites at once. Let the builders finish something first.
texte.bau.grund.room_too_big: That room would be too big. Split it up.
texte.bau.grund.no_world: The world is not ready yet.
texte.bau.hilfe.wand: Wall: drag a straight line along the tile edges. Gaps get walls; a line that is already all wall comes down instead. Doors stay where they are.
texte.bau.hilfe.tuer: Door: tap a wall of a building. Tap again for a gate, once more and it is a wall again. Nobody said architecture was decisive.
texte.bau.hilfe.dach: Roof: drag over a building. Roof on the first tile? Off it comes, and you have a courtyard. Otherwise it goes on. Free; the rain is not.
texte.bau.hilfe.huelle: Rebuild walls: tap a building. Every open edge gets its wall back, and a door if none is left.
texte.bau.zuLang: Too long. At most {n} walls at once; the masons have to sleep sometime.
texte.bau.vorschauDach: {n} × {m} tiles · release to open or close the roof
texte.bau.okWand: {n} walls planned for {g} gold. Good fences make obedient neighbours.
texte.bau.okWandAb: {n} walls torn down. Fresh air, free of charge.
texte.bau.okTuer.tuer: Door planned. Now they can leave. Or try.
texte.bau.okTuer.tor: Gate planned. Wide enough for a cart, or a crowd running away.
texte.bau.okTuer.wand: Walled up again. Whoever was outside stays outside.
texte.bau.okHuelleLeer: Nothing to rebuild. This one is already a proper box.
texte.bau.tippWand: Tap a wall, not the floor. The floor does not open.
texte.bau.tippHaus: Tap a building. Open fields have no walls to fix.
texte.bau.grund.dead_end: That would wall in the only way out. The builders like to go home in the evening.
texte.bau.grund.no_wall: No wall here. A door needs something to sit in.
texte.waren.leer: No goods yet. Finish your first storage; a starter supply of dubious origin will turn up.
texte.waren.zahl: Storages {l} · loose piles {s} · open orders {a} · delivered {g} · built in {v}
texte.waren.block.1: nobody is building. The workers are busy, or pretending to be.
texte.waren.block.2: no material left anywhere. Even the rats have stopped looking.
texte.waren.block.3: waiting for material. It is on somebody's shoulder, somewhere.
texte.waren.block.5: too far from your workers. They walk about 150 fields and not one step more.
texte.waren.block.4: nobody can get there. Build a way in, or teach them to climb.
texte.karren.fracht: Carrying {m} {w}. The ox carries, the driver supervises.
texte.karren.leer: Waiting for orders. The ox calls it a career.
texte.person.auf.0: Idle. He calls it resting his talents.
texte.person.auf.1: Fetching goods. Walking empty is the best part of the job.
texte.person.auf.3: Building. Most of the fingers are still attached.
texte.person.auf.4: Bringing goods back. Somebody changed their mind again.
texte.person.auf.w: Stuck. No way through, so he waits and blames the planner.
texte.person.faehig: Hauling {a} · Building {b} · Felling {c} · Sawing {d} · Cooking {e} · Hunting {f} · Water {g}
texte.probe.warenSucht: Goods probe: looking for flat ground. The workers hope there is none.
texte.probe.warenKeinPlatz: Goods probe: no free flat ground nearby. Scroll somewhere else and reload.
texte.probe.waren1: Goods probe: five workers build the first storage, without material and without thanks.
texte.probe.waren2: Goods probe: starter supply is in. Workshop and second storage ordered; now every plank has to be carried.
texte.probe.waren3: Goods probe: gates and road ordered. The ox carts will even out the storages. Open Goods and tap a worker.
texte.person.auf.5: Felling a tree. The tree had it coming.
texte.person.auf.6: Sawing logs into boards. Measures once, cuts whenever.
texte.person.auf.7: Cooking. Nobody asks what is in it, and he does not say.
texte.person.auf.8: Hunting. Creeping up on a deer with the grace of a falling wardrobe.
texte.person.auf.9: Drawing water. He tested it first; the fish did not complain.
texte.person.auf.10: Going for food and water. Work can wait, it always does.
texte.person.hunger.1: Hungry: works at half speed and lets everyone know.
texte.person.hunger.2: Thirsty: works at half speed and stares at puddles.
texte.person.hunger.3: Hungry and thirsty: half speed, full self-pity.
texte.ketten.ziel: Target stock: boards {a} · water {c} · meals {d} · logs {e} · meat {f}
texte.ketten.hin.1: No tree within reach of a storage. The axes are getting bored.
texte.ketten.hin.2: No river or lake within reach of a storage. Thirst will be educational.
texte.ketten.hin.4: No deer near the hunter's hut yet. They will come; they never learn either.
texte.ketten.hin.8: Boards are short: build a sawmill. The logs will not saw themselves.
texte.ketten.hin.16: Meals are short: build a kitchen. Raw deer is a hobby, not a diet.
texte.ketten.hin.32: Meat is short: build a hunter's hut. The deer are counting on it.
texte.ketten.hin.64: Every storage is full. Build another one or stop being so productive.
texte.ketten.hin.128: Somebody is hungry or thirsty and working at half speed.
texte.tier.zust.1: Wandering about, looking for better grass.
texte.tier.zust.2: Frozen still. Something is creeping up on it.
texte.markt.kopf: Day {tag} · {p} gold each · you have {g} gold
texte.markt.unterwegs: The trader is on his way with today's goods. The chains rattle before you see him.
texte.markt.leer: Sold out. The trader brings five new ones tomorrow; the road never runs dry.
texte.markt.zu: The market stall is still being set up.
texte.markt.gekauft: {n} is yours now. He looks thrilled, in the way a man in chains can look thrilled.
texte.markt.nein.gone: Too late. That one is gone.
texte.markt.nein.no_gold: Not enough gold. The trader laughs and keeps the chain.
texte.person.auf.11: Off to the arena. He walks like a man who has read the program.
texte.arena.zu: The arena is still being raked.
texte.arena.frei: No fight booked. The sand is waiting, and it is patient.
texte.arena.termin.kurz: Fight booked for day {tag} at noon.
texte.arena.zu0: They work until mid-morning, then walk over.
texte.arena.zu1: They are on their way. {da} of {n} at the gate.
texte.arena.zu2: The crowd is seated. {da} of {n} at the gate.
texte.arena.gebucht: Fight booked for day {tag} at noon. The undertaker has been told, just in case.
texte.arena.sieg: Victory. {g} gold for the purse, and the crowd goes home happy.
texte.arena.niederlage: Defeat. {g} gold anyway; the crowd paid to watch, not to win.
texte.arena.letzt.ab: Last fight: {s} {l}, called off. The crowd threw vegetables at nobody.
texte.arena.nein.busy: There is already a fight booked.
texte.arena.nein.no_arena: The arena is still being raked.
texte.person.auf.12: Laid up. He groans professionally and heals at the house's expense.
texte.person.ruht: Badly hurt. No work until he can stand without help.
texte.arena.frage: The crowd is seated and the men are on the sand.
texte.arena.frage.leise: Watch the fight, or let the clerk bring you the result?
texte.arena.rechnet: The fight is on. The clerk takes notes …
texte.arena.unfit: {n} is not fit to fight. Watch the fight to change the group.
texte.arena.nein.nobody2: Nobody of the group is left to fight.
texte.arena.bericht.geld: Purse {g} gold · {z} spectators paid {t} gold for tickets.
texte.arena.gefallen: {n} fell. The undertaker sends his regards and his bill.
texte.arena.gefallen.zahl: Fallen in this arena so far: {n}.
texte.leiche.info: He will lie here until tomorrow, so everyone can see what the purse costs. Then the cart comes.
texte.med.zu: The medicus is still unpacking his saws.
texte.med.keiner: Nobody needs stitching. Enjoy it; it never lasts.
texte.med.laedt: The medicus is looking them over…
texte.med.ok: {n} has been treated ({s}, {k} gold). The healing goes faster for the next four days.
texte.med.nein.no_gold: Not enough gold. The medicus does not do charity, only amputations.
texte.med.nein.gone: That patient has changed since the medicus looked; tap again.
texte.med.fehler: The medicus dropped his instruments. Try again.
texte.med.hilfe: Each treatment speeds up healing for four days, like in the old ludus. The price grows with the wounds.
texte.reich.niemand: No one rules here. The vultures keep the peace.
texte.person.arenaSatz.1: Calls the arena a waste of good blood. Means the blood.
texte.person.arenaSatz.2: Attends, but sits near the exit.
texte.person.arenaSatz.3: Watches the games the way he watches the rain.
texte.person.arenaSatz.4: Knows every champion by name, and most by price.
texte.person.arenaSatz.5: Has sold a province, a son and a harvest for better seats.
texte.chronik.gruendung.0: Founded by {founder}, who conquered {seat} and then, for tax purposes, everything else.
texte.chronik.gruendung.1: {founder} was crowned in {seat} after the other claimants fell down some stairs.
texte.chronik.gruendung.2: {founder} bought {seat} at auction and declared himself Prince before the bid cleared.
texte.chronik.gruendung.3: {seat} became a republic when the last king was voted out, then down a well.
texte.chronik.gruendung.4: Founded when three families of {seat} agreed on a price for everything, including each other.
texte.chronik.gruendung.5: {founder} heard a god speak in {seat}. The god has since been billed for the temple.
texte.chronik.gruendung.6: The clans met at {seat} to choose a chief. {founder} survived the meeting.
texte.chronik.gruendung.7: {founder} built a toll gate near {seat}, then a wall, then a castle around the toll gate.
texte.chronik.ereignis.1: The Great Famine was blamed on a goat, which was tried, convicted and eaten.
texte.chronik.ereignis.2: A border war over a single well lasted forty years. The well dried up in year two.
texte.chronik.ereignis.3: A plague arrived by ship and left with the tax records.
texte.chronik.ereignis.4: The treasury was lost at dice, won back at dice, and lost again for good measure.
texte.chronik.ereignis.5: A rebellion was crushed, then hired, then crushed again for asking for wages.
texte.chronik.ereignis.6: An earthquake levelled the old palace. The new one was built with the proceeds.
texte.chronik.ereignis.7: A prophet foretold the end of the realm. He was executed on schedule.
texte.chronik.ereignis.8: The realm once ruled the coast, until the coast was sold to pay for a parade.
texte.chronik.ereignis.9: Two heirs split the crown in half. The jeweller kept the middle.
texte.chronik.ereignis.10: A famous arena champion was crowned by the mob and deposed by a lion.
texte.chronik.ereignis.11: The census counted more dead voters than living ones. Both were taxed.
texte.chronik.ereignis.12: A dragon was reported, hunted, and found to be a large, offended lizard.
texte.chronik.heute.1: Today {ruler} rules from {seat} and trusts nobody, which experts call wise.
texte.chronik.heute.2: Today {ruler} rules from {seat}, mostly by not being in the room when things happen.
texte.chronik.heute.3: Today the realm is prosperous, peaceful and suspicious of both.
texte.chronik.heute.4: Today {ruler} owes money to everyone, and everyone is very polite to him about it.
texte.chronik.heute.5: Today the realm is famous for its games and infamous for paying for them.
texte.chronik.heute.6: Today {ruler} plans a great war, as soon as someone remembers against whom.
texte.chronik.heute.7: Today the people of {seat} are loyal, well fed and closely watched.
texte.chronik.heute.8: Today {ruler} keeps three heirs, two poison tasters and one honest adviser, for decoration.
texte.chronik.vasall: Since then it has bent the knee to the {lord}, and its knees have never recovered.
